headline: The ACME client ships. pki.acme drives the full RFC 8555 certificate-issuance flow over the shared node:https transport.
summary: pki.acme.client is a stateful ACME client that walks a live CA directory end to end: fetch the directory, register or find an account, place an order, answer its authorizations, finalize with a CSR, and download the issued chain, plus certificate revocation, account key rotation, account and authorization deactivation, and ARI renewal-info. It composes the shipped ACME message layer (the JWS builders, object validators, and state machines) and the shared pki.transport, owning only session state (the fetched directory, the single-use nonce pool, and the account URL). It is fail-closed by default: HTTPS is required for every request, the default transport needs an explicit trust anchor, each request carries a fresh anti-replay nonce, reads are POST-as-GET, polling is bounded, and every response body is size-capped.

Added: pki.acme.client(directoryUrl, opts) is a stateful RFC 8555 ACME client over the shared pki.transport. newAccount / newOrder / getOrder / getAuthorization / getChallenge / respondToChallenge / finalize / pollOrder / pollAuthorization / downloadCertificate drive the issuance flow; revokeCert (RFC 8555 sec. 7.6, account-key or certificate-key signed), keyChange (sec. 7.3.5 account key rotation), deactivateAccount / deactivateAuthorization, and renewalInfo (ARI, RFC 9773) round out the account and certificate lifecycle. Signs every request with the account key (opts.accountKey / accountJwk / alg); reads are POST-as-GET; a problem+json response surfaces as a typed acme/server-problem.

Fail-closed transport defaults for the client: HTTPS is required for the directory URL and every server-returned URL (acme/insecure-url), the default transport rejects a connection with no explicit trust anchor unless tls.useSystemStore is set (acme/no-trust-anchors), each JWS carries a fresh single-use nonce with a bounded badNonce retry, the poll loop is bounded by maxPolls and a total-wait budget and sleeps on a Retry-After via an injectable sleeper, and every response body is capped (acme/response-too-large).
Fixed: The EST enrollment client now measures a string response body as UTF-8 (the width it is decoded at), so a non-ASCII body cannot undercount its byte length and slip past the response-size cap. The built-in node:https transport was unaffected (it returns raw bytes); this hardens a custom injected transport that returns string bodies.
